transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (Redwood AE), Marco Rivera (Redwood SE), Anya Sokolov (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Celestia ML Infra), Tom Howard (Head of ML), Elena Gomez (SRE), Marcus Lee (Data Scientist)

Summary:
Redwood ran through quantization tradeoffs (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) and practical runtime/perf impacts for Celestia's on-device inference plans. Customer wants guidance on accuracy regressions, KV cache impacts, batching strategies, and VPC/on-prem deployment considerations for a pilot.

Topics:
- Accuracy tradeoffs: GPTQ vs AWQ vs 8-bit float
- Latency and throughput on dedicated inference nodes
- KV cache behavior with quantized weights and long context windows
- Batching policies for low-latency robotics control loop
- VPC/on-prem deployment, KMS & audit logs

Transcript body:
00:00:02 - Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intro. I'm Jasmine, AE at Redwood, with Marco and Anya from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
00:00:10 - Priya: Hey, good, thanks. We are excited. We have a couple of production constraints to run through.
00:00:18 - Marco: Great. We planned to cover quantization strategies — INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ — and then runtime impacts: batching, KV cache, and on-prem notes. We can jump to the part you care about most.
00:00:29 - Tom: For us, main asks: can we get near-floating-point accuracy with 8-bit-ish formats, what are the latency hits, and how does KV cache behave with longer context? Also curious about on-prem packaging and network isolation.
00:00:42 - Marco: Makes sense. Quick overview: INT8 gives strong throughput improvements but often needs per-channel calibration or GPTQ-style post-training quant; AWQ is newer, often better on some LLMs for accuracy vs size, and FP8 might be an option on hardware that supports it with better dynamic range.
00:01:05 - Elena: Sorry, FP8? We don't have FP8-capable HW yet in our DCs; most of our infra is Ampere A100 and a couple of older T4s.
00:01:13 - Anya: That matters. FP8 really helps when hardware supports it (NVIDIA H100, L4 variants), but on A100 you'd rely on INT8/GPTQ/AWQ paths in the runtime.
00:01:25 - Marcus: Our inference profile is short control prompts ~ 128 tokens then streaming outputs, real-time constraints, target P95 latency < 120ms. Throughput isn't huge, but tail latency is critical.
00:01:39 - Marco: That's useful. Tail latency constraints change batching strategy: small max batch and aggressive SLO-based preemption. For quantized models, per-token computation is faster, but kernel selection and cache warm-up still drive P95.
00:01:56 - Priya: On KV cache: when we quantize, do we keep KV cache in FP16 or quantize that too? Any accuracy tradeoffs?
00:02:05 - Marco: Good question. Redwood's runtime keeps KV cache in higher precision (FP16) by default to avoid compounding quantization error across long contexts. We've seen significant regressions if you quantize both weights and KV cache to INT8 on long sequence lengths — hallucination and degradation in next-token probabilities.
00:02:24 - Tom: So default is weights quantized but cache FP16. Does that have big memory overhead?
00:02:30 - Marco: It's a tradeoff: FP16 cache costs memory but is cheaper than re-running prefixes. For your 128-token typical profile it's reasonable; for very long contexts (2k+) you need to size memory accordingly or consider prefix caching on disk with fast NVMe and smart sharding.
00:02:47 - Marcus: If we keep cache FP16 and weights INT8, does latency still improve much?
00:02:52 - Anya: Yes — kernel speedups for matmuls still dominate. On A100, INT8 kernels can be 2-3x faster for the attention matmul paths depending on seq len and batch size; however, for small batches the kernel launch overhead and data movement can reduce that benefit.
00:03:10 - Priya: You mentioned GPTQ vs AWQ — which should we prefer for our models? We use a fine-tuned Llama-variant at 13B.
00:03:19 - Marco: Empirically, GPTQ-style per-layer transposed quant tends to preserve accuracy well for many Llama-family weights. AWQ has shown advantages on some models with fewer calibration steps and smaller accuracy drop for some instruction-tuned models, but it's model-dependent. We usually run both automated evals on your prompt set.
00:03:37 - Tom: How do you measure accuracy regressions? We need concrete thresholds to accept a quantized model.
00:03:43 - Anya: We run a holdout prompt set (you provide ~1k prompts plus edge cases) and compute metrics: exact-match for structured outputs, Rouge/BLEU for longer text, and embedding-similarity deltas for semantic drift. We flag regressions > 2-3% on critical metrics, but it's configurable.
00:04:01 - Marco: Also qualitative checks for instruction-following failures. With GPTQ sometimes you see a few hallucinations unless you fine-tune or use per-channel scale corrections.
00:04:10 - Priya: For our controls, 2% drop is the max. Can you run GPTQ + AWQ and give diff?
00:04:15 - Jasmine: Yep, that's part of the pilot: Marco will prepare an accuracy matrix comparing FP16 baseline, GPTQ INT8, AWQ, and a hybrid FP8 where available. We'll include latency and memory numbers.
00:04:28 - Elena: On the VPC side: we need KMS, audit logs, SSO, RBAC. If we go on-prem, how does Redwood handle key management?
00:04:36 - Marco: For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM via KMIP or cloud KMS APIs, all traffic goes over customer VPC peering or private link, and we ship an on-prem agent if you choose air-gapped mode. Audit logs are configurable and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
00:04:52 - Tom: Are there extra latency costs for VPC peering in a cross-region setup?
00:04:57 - Anya: Network latency can dominate if model hosts are remote; we recommend colocating inference nodes in the same region or on-prem for low-latency robotics control. Redwood supports private deployments so compute can be local.
00:05:10 - Marcus: Any specific kernel-level gotchas if we run GPTQ models on A100 versus H100?
00:05:16 - Marco: H100 has native FP8 and new INT8 tensor core paths; some AWQ kernels are faster there. On A100 you rely on optimized INT8 kernels and mixed-precision. We recommend profiling with your sequence lengths — we can run microbenchmarks.
00:05:31 - Priya: Can you share a sample benchmark config?
00:05:33 - Jasmine: We'll send the benchmark config, includes representative prompts, sequence lengths, batch sizes 1/2/4/8, and SLO targets.
00:05:40 - Tom: About batching: we worry batching will increase tail latency unpredictably. For a robotics control loop, we'd prefer deterministic latency. How do you handle that?
00:05:48 - Marco: Redwood's runtime supports SLO-aware batching: it will flush batches when the oldest request approaches the latency SLO. Also supports priority lanes and preemption for AI control traffic. For your use-case we recommend max batch 4 with batch timeout tuned to your P95 target. We'll share recommended policies.
00:06:06 - Marcus: What about cache warming — cold start is bad for us. Any mitigations?
00:06:10 - Anya: We support prefix warming, keep-alive drivers, and pinning model instances in Dedicated deployments so warm caches persist. Also automatic request routing to warmed nodes for hot keys.
00:06:22 - Priya: If we do a hybrid quant strategy (some layers INT8, some kept FP16), how is that configured? Do you maintain model variants?
00:06:31 - Marco: Exactly. We produce model variants and tag them (e.g., fp16, int8_gptq, awq_hybrid) and runtime routes by policy. You can A/B test and roll back. For hybrids it's usually last n layers left in FP16, earlier layers quantized.
00:06:46 - Tom: Is there tooling to re-run evaluations after we change quantization thresholds?
00:06:50 - Anya: Yes, our Optimize toolkit can auto-sweep quantization granularity and produce accuracy vs latency curves. We'll include the initial sweep in the pilot.
00:06:58 - Priya: Any mention of tokenization or prompt pre-processing affecting quantization?
00:07:03 - Marco: Indirectly: change in tokenization length distribution affects batch packing and cache hit rates. Also longer prefixes increase chance of quantization drift in chained generations; that's why we keep KV in higher precision.
00:07:17 - Marcus: For a 13B Llama, what order-of-magnitude memory and latency improvements should we expect with INT8 vs FP16 on A100?
00:07:25 - Marco: Roughly memory can drop ~40-50% for weight storage. Latency per token might improve 1.5x-2.2x depending on sequence and batch. But end-to-end tail latency improvement lower due to I/O and cache warmups.
00:07:39 - Elena: Are there known failure modes where quantized model behaves worse at inference time even though eval metrics look fine?
00:07:46 - Marco: Yes: some instruction-following stresses or rare tokens can flip behaviour. That's why we do both automated evals and manual spot-checks on worst-case prompts. Also watch for temperature/decoding interplay — sampling hyperparams can amplify small distribution shifts.
00:08:01 - Tom: On observability: how granular are the traces we get? We want per-token latency breakdowns.
00:08:07 - Anya: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, kernel-level timings, KV cache hit/miss stats, and per-route cost. We can also export traces to your tracing backend.
00:08:19 - Priya: For pilot, we want a 3-week run with our 1k prompts, compare FP16 baseline vs GPTQ and AWQ, and then pick one for a canary deployment. Is that realistic?
00:08:29 - Jasmine: Yes. Typical pilot: week 1 - onboarding & dataset; week 2 - quantization sweeps and benchmarks; week 3 - canary with dedicated nodes. We'll propose a timeline in the follow-up.
00:08:40 - Tom: Pricing for dedicated capacity — can you ballpark?
00:08:44 - Jasmine: We'll send an estimate. It depends on committed hours and node types. We'll provide both on-demand and reserved pricing.
00:08:52 - Marcus: Any legal/compliance concerns for on-prem deployment — e.g., audit logs retention and encrypted at rest?
00:08:58 - Marco: Audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, retention configurable. Data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys in Private. We'll include details in the security pack.
00:09:08 - Elena: One more kernel question: if we mix FP16 cache and INT8 weights, does the runtime do conversions per token that might add CPU overhead?
00:09:15 - Marco: There's minimal conversion cost; modern runtimes keep activations and cache aligned in GPU memory and use mixed-precision kernels. The overhead is minor versus matmul costs.
00:09:26 - Priya: Great.
00:09:30 - [discussion continues with some cross-talk, detailed clarifications and microbenchmark talk]
00:25:02 - Marco: I'll call out a few microbenchmarks we recommend: 1) single-stream latency (batch=1) for 64/128 seed tokens; 2) batched throughput sweep b=1..8; 3) long context 2k prefix evaluation for KV retention; 4) accuracy sweep across your 1k prompts.
00:25:25 - Marcus: For the accuracy sweep, please also include few-shot instruction examples.
00:25:30 - Anya: Will do.
00:25:34 - Tom: Are there known quantization libraries you use under the hood? We care about reproducibility.
00:25:40 - Marco: We leverage open-source GPTQ forks and AWQ implementations where applicable, plus our internal quantization toolchain that wraps them and produces runtime-compatible kernels. We track exact commits and seed values for reproducibility.
00:25:55 - Priya: Perfect.
00:26:00 - Jasmine: Quick recap of next steps: Marco will run initial sweep and produce an accuracy matrix, I'll send security and benchmark configs, schedule kickoff for pilot next Tuesday?
00:26:10 - Priya: Tuesday works.
00:26:12 - Tom: Agree.
00:26:15 - Marcus: Thanks everyone.
00:26:18 - Jasmine: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the matrix.
